# Microsoft Azure Azure.ResourceManager.ManagedNetworkFabric management client library for .NET

Managed Network Fabric RP exposes APIs to enable bootstrapping and configuration of devices of Network Fabric in Telco premises. This enables programming the network devices for enabling management infrastructure and tenant workloads. 

This library follows the [new Azure SDK guidelines](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/general_introduction.html), and provides many core capabilities:

    - Support MSAL.NET, Azure.Identity is out of box for supporting MSAL.NET.
    - Support [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/) for distributed tracing.
    - HTTP pipeline with custom policies.
    - Better error-handling.
    - Support uniform telemetry across all languages.

## Getting started 

### Install the package

Install the Microsoft Azure Azure.ResourceManager.ManagedNetworkFabric management library for .NET with [NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/):

```dotnetcli
dotnet add package Azure.ResourceManager.ManagedNetworkFabric
```

### Prerequisites

* You must have an [Microsoft Azure subscription](https://azure.microsoft.com/free/dotnet/).

### Authenticate the Client

To create an authenticated client and start interacting with Microsoft Azure resources, see the [quickstart guide here](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).

## Key concepts

Key concepts of the Microsoft Azure SDK for .NET can be found [here](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/dotnet_introduction.html)

## Documentation

Documentation is available to help you learn how to use this package:

- [Quickstart](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).
- [API References](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/?view=azure-dotnet).
- [Authentication](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/sdk/identity/Azure.Identity/README.md).

## Examples

Code samples for using the management library for .NET can be found in the following locations
- [.NET Management Library Code Samples](https://aka.ms/azuresdk-net-mgmt-samples)

## Troubleshooting

-   File an issue via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/issues).
-   Check [previous questions](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/azure+.net) or ask new ones on Stack Overflow using Azure and .NET tags.

## Next steps

For more information about Microsoft Azure SDK, see [this website](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/).

## Contributing

For details on contributing to this repository, see the [contributing
guide][cg].

This project welcomes contributions and suggestions. Most contributions
require you to agree to a Contributor License Agreement (CLA) declaring
that you have the right to, and actually do, grant us the rights to use
your contribution. For details, visit <https://cla.microsoft.com>.

When you submit a pull request, a CLA-bot will automatically determine
whether you need to provide a CLA and decorate the PR appropriately
(for example, label, comment). Follow the instructions provided by the
bot. You'll only need to do this action once across all repositories
using our CLA.

This project has adopted the [Microsoft Open Source Code of Conduct][coc]. For
more information, see the [Code of Conduct FAQ][coc_faq] or contact
<opencode@microsoft.com> with any other questions or comments.

proposals.explanation: The suppressed IPAddress-shaped factory is replaced with a hidden method that constructs NetworkFabricInternetGatewayData, substitutes a ChangeTrackingDictionary for null tags and conditionally builds nested InternetGatewayProperties with LastOperationProperties. Its body does not forward the iPv4Address or typePropertiesType arguments: the displayed nested constructor receives default in the address slot and internetGatewayType in two adjacent type slots.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete manually implemented factory body, EditorBrowsable attribute and matching CodeGenSuppress signature are supplied from src/Customize, not a generated model-factory file.

It defaults null tags to a ChangeTrackingDictionary and either omits nested InternetGatewayProperties or constructs them using the supplied iPV4Address string, typePropertiesType and remaining captured arguments, with default values for the additional nested slots.

proposals.subtype: Operation-status model factory with reordered resource ID and materialized operations
proposals.explanation: A handwritten factory exposes resourceId immediately after id but supplies it as the final constructor argument when creating NetworkFabricOperationStatusResult. It also materializes the supplied operations sequence with ToList, first replacing a null sequence with an empty ChangeTrackingList.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: This public static model-construction method and its explicit argument rearrangement and sequence conversion are implemented in src/Customize outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete BGP model-factory overloads retained as throwing stubs
proposals.explanation: Both captured InternalNetworkBgpConfiguration factory overloads remain public but hidden and obsolete. The eleven-parameter form and the fourteen-parameter form with BMP and cross-address-family session settings both immediately throw NotSupportedException directing callers to BgpConfiguration, rather than constructing a result.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The two explicit obsolete method bodies are in the handwritten factory partial, and their throwing behavior is directly visible without relying on migration comments.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete VPN factory with retired OptionA parameter type
proposals.explanation: The public VpnConfigurationProperties factory accepting VpnConfigurationOptionAProperties is hidden and obsolete and immediately throws NotSupportedException. Both the attribute and exception direct callers to an overload using VpnOptionAProperties; that destination overload is not supplied.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: This non-generated factory method explicitly supplies obsolete metadata and a throwing implementation in src/Customize.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete static-route model factory retained as a throwing stub
proposals.explanation: The hidden, obsolete InternalNetworkStaticRouteConfiguration factory still exposes its BFD, IPv4/IPv6 route and extension parameters, but its entire implementation throws NotSupportedException directing callers to StaticRouteConfiguration.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The obsolete declaration and complete non-generated throwing factory body are captured in src/Customize.

proposals.subtype: Suppressed internal-network factory replaced with obsolete throwing overloads
proposals.explanation: The captured factory suppresses the internal-network signature containing InternalNetworkBgpConfiguration and InternalNetworkStaticRouteConfiguration. Its matching optional-parameter implementation and the other captured overload with separate import/export route-policy IDs are hidden, obsolete and immediately throw NotSupportedException directing callers to a BgpConfiguration-based overload. The suppression and its matching stub are one coupled API customization, not two findings.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The exact CodeGenSuppress parameter sequence and both explicit obsolete throwing bodies are visible in the handwritten factory partial outside Generated.

proposals.explanation: The otherwise empty handwritten AzureResourceManagerManagedNetworkFabricContext partial carries ModelReaderWriterBuildable attributes for the listed configuration, patch and operation-status models. proposals.explanation: BgpConfiguration adds a hidden public parameterless constructor that delegates to this(default). The destination constructor is not captured, so this finding does not assert which value or validation behavior that overload ultimately uses.

proposals.subtype: Hidden obsolete BGP wrapper type with forwarding constructors
proposals.explanation: InternalNetworkBgpConfiguration is a public, hidden, obsolete subclass of BgpConfiguration. Its public parameterless constructor delegates a default nullable long, its peer-ASN constructor forwards to the base, and its internal all-fields constructor forwards the displayed configuration and additional-data arguments to the base constructor. This is a concrete compatibility-shaped type surface, not proof of an earlier release's implementation.

proposals.explanation: The derived model's explicit IJsonModel and IPersistableModel implementations delegate writing and format selection to the BgpConfiguration interfaces. proposals.subtype: Hidden obsolete static-route wrapper type with forwarding construction
proposals.explanation: InternalNetworkStaticRouteConfiguration remains a public, hidden, obsolete subclass of StaticRouteConfiguration with a public parameterless constructor. Its internal constructor forwards BFD configuration, IPv4/IPv6 route lists, extension and additional-data arguments to the base. The annotations explicitly name StaticRouteConfiguration as the replacement without establishing the SDK's historical behavior.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: This non-generated model partial contains an explicit base type, retained public construction surface and a manually written internal base-constructor forwarding call.

proposals.subtype: Derived static-route model JSON and persistence interface bridge
proposals.explanation: The derived static-route model implements its JSON and persistence interfaces by delegating writing and format selection to StaticRouteConfiguration. Its two Create methods reconstruct the derived type with a null-aware helper that transfers BFD configuration, both route lists and extension while passing null for additionalBinaryDataProperties; it does not explicitly clone the route lists.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The explicit interface delegation and derived-type reconstruction are handwritten in src/Customize/Models, independently of any unavailable base serialization implementation.

decisions.reason: The active CodeGenSuppress attribute on the handwritten factory partial names this exact NetworkFabricData factory signature at line 19. Suppressing that generated surface is a distinct model API change; the excerpt does not establish a replacement or why it was needed.

Line 22 explicitly suppresses the NetworkTapData factory signature in the handwritten Customize file. The proposed explanation correctly limits itself to that signature rather than claiming an uncaptured replacement.

Line 24 suppresses the named NetworkToNetworkInterconnectData factory signature, including the OptionB layer-three type. This is handwritten member-suppression metadata, not evidence that any particular replacement was generated or implemented.

The matching suppression at line 20 and complete handwritten overload at lines 30-52 support a replacement model factory. Its body does not reference iPv4Address or typePropertiesType; the address constructor argument is default and both adjacent type arguments use internetGatewayType. This observation is not a claim about historical cause or runtime intent.

The string-address signature is separately suppressed at line 21 and implemented at lines 56-78; its body passes the string address into nested properties and substitutes an empty change-tracking dictionary for null tags. The two overloads have different signatures and behavior.

Lines 82-92 show a handwritten output-model factory moving resourceId from its second public parameter to the last constructor argument and materializing operations after null substitution. The existing model-factory-method pattern fits this reusable API shape.

Both captured BGP factory overloads are annotated obsolete and hidden and immediately throw NotSupportedException at lines 107-112 and 130-136. They form one retained, unusable compatibility-shaped factory surface; no successful forwarding is claimed.

Lines 145-150 show a hidden obsolete VPN factory overload with the older OptionA type and an unconditional NotSupportedException. The cited replacement overload is mentioned by its diagnostic text, not independently established by the capture.

Lines 158-163 contain the complete hidden obsolete static-route factory overload and its unconditional NotSupportedException. The compatibility-shim pattern describes this concrete retained API surface without claiming it remains operational.

The CodeGenSuppress signature at line 23 corresponds to the optional-parameter internal-network factory at lines 199-203; both that and the separately captured older overload at lines 189-194 throw. Counting these coupled obsolete signatures as one factory behavior avoids a duplicate finding for the suppression alone.

Lines 214-219 show a complete hidden obsolete seven-argument factory method that unconditionally throws and points to OptionBLayer3Configuration. The excerpt ends before the next method declaration, so the finding correctly refrains from describing it.

The non-generated context partial has a substantial block of ModelReaderWriterBuildable declarations at lines 12-42 rather than being an empty scaffold. They explicitly alter the declared serialization-model registration surface; the generated implementation and runtime effects remain uncaptured. No catalog entry specifically describes these context registrations.

Lines 16-20 add a hidden parameterless BgpConfiguration constructor that calls another overload with default. This is a concrete model-constructor addition; comments about migration and the uncaptured destination body are not necessary to establish the API shape.

Lines 15-16 explicitly add a computed public property exposing a nested failed-devices value through an IReadOnlyList<string> as-cast. An as-cast can produce null and does not create an immutable copy, as the proposal correctly states.

The handwritten property at lines 16-26 reads the nested IPv4 route-policy ID and creates a nested policy object before setting that ID when needed. It is an actual model-property alias with setter behavior rather than a mere annotation.

Lines 19-22 add a hidden public single-ResourceIdentifier constructor forwarding its argument and default to an uncaptured two-argument overload. This supports an alternative constructor but not the historical release or destination validation assertions in the comments.

Lines 16-19 add a hidden parameterless ExternalNetworkOptionAProperties constructor forwarding two default arguments. The model-alternate-constructors pattern matches; the missing destination body prevents stronger runtime or historical claims.

Lines 18-37 define the public hidden obsolete derived BGP type and its three explicit constructors, including a base-forwarding internal overload. This is a distinct model-compatibility surface from its separately captured JSON/persistence methods; the comment alone does not establish release history.

Lines 39-70 implement explicit derived-model JSON and persistence interfaces by delegating through BgpConfiguration and reconstructing the derived instance from visible base properties, passing null for additional binary data. This bridge is not a handwritten property-by-property JSON writer, and its distinct response-only pattern captures that difference.

Lines 18-31 define a hidden obsolete public subclass with a public parameterless constructor and an internal constructor forwarding to StaticRouteConfiguration. The retained model type is a separate API-surface behavior from its interface bridge.

Lines 33-54 show explicit JSON and persistence delegation to the static-route base plus a helper rebuilding the derived model from visible fields. The route lists are passed through without an explicit clone, and no assertion about unavailable base serializer internals is needed.

Lines 15-16 add a computed BFD status property that reads a nested list through an IReadOnlyList<T> as-cast. This is a handwritten flattened property alias, not a copied collection or an LRO polling implementation.

Lines 15-16 add the analogous BGP status property, with its own distinct model type and element type. Its null-aware nested-list cast supports the model-property-alias finding without implying immutable storage.

limitations: Coverage is partial: 11 captures from 1207 eligible files among 1240 discovered files. Ten captures are complete files and the model factory is only lines 1-223; all 82 skipped inventory entries were read as coverage metadata, not as evidence of their uncaptured contents.

The factory excerpt ends at an EditorBrowsable attribute for a further overload. Its missing declaration/body and all uncaptured factory replacements, generated counterparts, serializers, operation sources and the remaining customization files are not assessed. An inventory path or a context registration does not establish a customization in an uncaptured file.

The supplied README, project and TypeSpec location identify package and generation context but do not supply the referenced specification, generator implementation, previous releases or current destination constructor bodies. No external URL, TypeSpec issue, historical compatibility claim or generator-defect explanation was independently verified.

The two BGP factory overloads with the same throwing retirement behavior are one finding, as are the two captured internal-network factory retirement overloads together with their matching suppression. Derived-type declarations/constructors are grouped as type-surface customizations, separately from their explicit serialization bridges, to avoid counting the same behavior twice.

The generated destination constructors and base serializers are unavailable, so delegating constructor and serialization findings describe the displayed call and reconstruction shapes, not proven successful execution or preservation of unshown data. No generated LRO poller, underlying paging implementation or absence of other customizations is inferred from this bounded evidence. The two response-only serialization/context pattern IDs describe the observed reusable shapes without changing the frozen pattern catalog; generatorAddressable judgments are plausibility assessments, not measured current generator capabilities.

This is an AI review of only the eleven supplied captured source texts. The factory capture ends at line 223, mid-file; no assertion is made about subsequent overloads, uncaptured generated counterparts, or uncaptured SDK implementations.

Coverage is partial: 11 of 1207 eligible files were captured, the factory is excerpted, and the supplied skipped inventory includes other Customize files. No absence or exhaustive-discovery conclusion follows from zero omissions in this bounded evidence.

The captured evidence items are marked unknown provenance; their paths under src/Customize and their concrete suppression attributes, constructors, properties, interfaces and factory bodies support handwritten-customization judgments under the supplied .NET guidelines, not independent historical verification.

Compatibility comments and diagnostics do not establish past releases or root causes; generatorAddressable yes is a plausibility judgment about reusable shapes, not evidence of an existing generator capability. No captured ordinary ArmOperation forwarding or custom polling behavior warrants an LRO finding.
